variants.name: Next.js
variants.how: React Server Components: render to the RSC payload, then render that to HTML; the payload is inlined for hydration; static shell + streamed holes (Partial Prerendering); gzip in Node by default.

variants.name: Next.js (tuned)
variants.how: Plain Next.js after profiling, still no caching: cacheComponents/Partial Prerendering off (one dynamic render instead of a staged render plus a prefetch render), the post card as a Client Component (props instead of a rendered tree in the RSC payload), V8 heap sized for the container.

variants.name: Next.js on Bun
variants.how: The same Next.js app and production build as Next.js; only the runtime changes: the standalone server.js runs on Bun instead of Node.

variants.name: Next.js cached
variants.how: Same app with 'use cache' and tag invalidation: post pages are stored after the first visit; the feed still renders per request from cached data.

variants.name: Next.js smart cache
variants.how: Whole feed page stored and regenerated every 15 s (never forced); post pages stored until edited; like counts fetched by the browser straight from the API. The server mostly serves stored HTML.

variants.name: Next.js full cache
variants.how: Whole feed page stored and regenerated every 30 s (never forced); post pages stored until edited; like counts only from the stored pages. The ceiling of Next.js caching.

variants.name: Remix (React Router 7)
variants.how: Loaders, then one React renderToPipeableStream pass; loader data embedded for hydration (~6.8 KB); Express server with gzip and per-request logging on by default.

variants.name: TanStack Start
variants.how: Loaders fill a per-request TanStack Query cache, one streaming React render; dehydrated query data embedded (~7 KB).

variants.name: SvelteKit
variants.how: Compiled Svelte components render by string concatenation; load data serialized into the page; whole page, then send.

variants.name: Nuxt
variants.how: Vue renderToString via Nitro/h3; useFetch calls the server's own API handler in-process; payload (~4.2 KB) embedded for hydration.

variants.name: SolidStart
variants.how: Solid's compiled SSR templates (string building with hydration keys), streaming; query data serialized (~4.8 KB).

variants.name: Qwik City
variants.how: Renders HTML and serializes component state for resumability (~12-13 KB of state); streamed; CSS inlined.

variants.name: Angular
variants.how: Builds a server-side DOM per request, then serializes it; hydration annotations, event replay and the HttpClient transfer cache embedded.

variants.name: Astro
variants.how: Server-rendered .astro templates with no client framework (zero JS); HTML forms via Astro Actions; CSS inlined.

variants.name: Express + EJS
variants.how: EJS templates compiled to JS functions once; render = string concatenation; nothing else. The Node baseline.

variants.name: Express + Nunjucks
variants.how: The same Express app with Jinja2-style Nunjucks templates (inheritance, includes, autoescape) instead of EJS; compiled once in production.

variants.name: Flask + Jinja2
variants.how: Jinja2 templates compiled to Python once; 3 sync gunicorn workers (one request each, Connection: close on every response).

variants.name: Django
variants.how: Django templates (node tree evaluation) behind the middleware stack; CSRF tokens; 3 sync gunicorn workers.

variants.name: ASP.NET Core Razor
variants.how: Razor views compiled to C# at build time; Kestrel; antiforgery tokens in every form (~4.6 KB of the feed).

variants.name: Laravel + Blade
variants.how: PHP-FPM (10 workers) behind nginx: the framework boots on every request; file sessions for CSRF; OPcache on.

variants.name: Spring Boot + Thymeleaf
variants.how: Thymeleaf evaluates templates per request over Tomcat's thread-per-request model; JVM defaults (SerialGC, 512 MB max heap).

variants.name: Rust Axum + Askama
variants.how: Askama compiles templates into Rust code at build time; render = writing into one pre-sized String; Tokio.

estimate.why: 30,000-user hold at 54% web CPU, 51% API CPU, 1,053 MiB: CPU reaches 95% near 52,000, memory (~33 KB per connection) runs out near 58,000, the shared API near 56,000

variants.name: Next.js on Deno
variants.how: The same Next.js app and production build as Next.js; the standalone server.js runs on Deno's Node compatibility layer.

variants.name: Next.js + nginx microcache
variants.how: Plain Next.js behind an nginx proxy_cache in the same box: anonymous feed cached 1 s, post pages 5 s; writes and logged-in users bypass it.

variants.name: Express + Nunjucks on Bun
variants.how: The same app and dependencies as Express + Nunjucks; only the runtime changes: server.js runs on Bun instead of Node.

variants.name: Hono JSX on Node
variants.how: Hono's server-only JSX renders components straight to an HTML string; no client framework, no hydration.

variants.name: Hono JSX on Bun
variants.how: The same Hono JSX app on Bun's native HTTP server.

variants.name: HonoX on Bun
variants.how: Hono's metaframework: file-based routes, hono/jsx rendered to a string, one island (the like button) hydrated in the browser; Vite build served by Bun.

variants.name: Go html/template
variants.how: net/http + html/template parsed once at startup; contextual autoescaping by reflection over the data; GOMAXPROCS 2 (Go's floor).

variants.name: Rails + ERB
variants.how: Rails 8 production defaults: one Puma process with 3 threads, ERB partials, cookie session + per-form CSRF tokens, request logging at info.

variants.name: Phoenix + HEEx
variants.how: Controllers render HEEx function components into iodata (no string concatenation); Bandit; cookie session + CSRF; gzip on by default.

variants.name: Laravel Octane
variants.how: The same Laravel app kept booted between requests by Octane on FrankenPHP (2 workers); no per-request framework boot, no nginx/FastCGI hop.

variants.name: Laravel Octane (tuned)
variants.how: Laravel Octane after profiling: keep-alive to the API, cookie sessions instead of files, no XSRF cookie, Blade timestamp checks off, fewer Octane listeners, OPcache JIT, post card as an @include.

variants.name: Leptos SSR
variants.how: Rust components rendered on the server (async mode) with hydration data for the WASM client; the full-stack Rust counterpart to Next.js.

variants.name: SvelteKit (fixed)
variants.how: SvelteKit with one line moved: the date formatter (Intl.DateTimeFormat) is created once per process instead of once per post card.

variants.name: Astro (fixed)
variants.how: Astro with one line moved: the date formatter (Intl.DateTimeFormat) is created once per process instead of once per post card.

variants.name: Spring Boot (AOT cache)
variants.how: Spring with the JDK 25 AOT cache (Spring Boot's documented recipe), so a fresh container isn't stuck JIT-compiling during its first minute.

variants.name: Django (tuned)
variants.how: Django with its built-in Jinja2 backend and a precompiled standard library (the 2 s healthcheck was recompiling urllib/email every time).

variants.name: Flask (precompiled stdlib)
variants.how: Flask with only a precompiled standard library, so the 2 s healthcheck stops recompiling urllib/email from source (~20% of the CPU budget).

variants.name: ASP.NET (tuned)
variants.how: ASP.NET with thread-pool spinning off, precompiled (ReadyToRun) publish, background GC off and invariant globalization.

variants.name: React Router 7 on Bun
variants.how: The same React Router 7 app as remix, served by Bun.serve through react-router's Web Request/Response handler (no Express, no gzip, no request log).

variants.name: Next.js static (CSR)
variants.how: Static HTML/JS from nginx; the browser fetches JSON through nginx's /api proxy and renders it. The server renders nothing.

estimate.why: one 30,000-user run, p95 41 ms: nginx (the web box) at 67% of its vCPU, the API at 47%: nginx reaches 95% near 42,000-43,000, the API near 60,000
